My own reverse DCF (WACC 7.5%, terminal growth 2.5%, base FCF = FY2025 actual $956m) implies ~3.8%/year firm-level FCF growth for 10 years. A reasonable base case (2-4%/year global can-volume growth plus modest margin/mix improvement) is ~4-5%/year, so implied growth sits at or slightly below base case (implied_vs_base = below), satisfying the INCLUDE threshold, though with a thinner margin of safety than WM or AMCR's reverse-DCF reads.

kill: Adjusted diluted EPS guidance is cut at any quarterly release (breaking the current raise streak).
A further goodwill/asset impairment exceeding $150m is booked in any single quarter (a fourth consecutive year of the PharmaLex-style pattern).
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 2.5x without a disclosed, value-accretive reason.
U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment revenue growth falls below 3% for two consecutive quarters (below even the cut 4-6% FY26 guide).
The "Other" segment strategic-alternatives review results in a divestiture loss exceeding $200m versus carrying value.
adverse: Three consecutive fiscal years of goodwill/asset impairments concentrated in PharmaLex/Other: $418.0m (Q4 FY2024), $723.9m (Q4 FY2025), $249.5m (FY2026-to-date)
Total debt nearly doubled in two quarters ($7.92bn at 2025-12-31 to $11.72bn at 2026-06-30) to fund the debt-financed step-up acquisition of OneOncology
FY2026 revenue-growth guidance was cut from 7-9% to 4-6% (both total company and the U.S. Healthcare Solutions segment) even as adjusted EPS guidance was raised over the same period
rows.thesis: Drug wholesaler with a growing specialty-oncology business, raising profit guidance every quarter despite a real pattern of goodwill write-downs.

val_consistency.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for COR, so there is nothing to reconcile against; this analyst's independent reverse DCF (WACC 7.5-9.0%, FY2026 guided adjusted-EPS midpoint $17.85, terminal growth 2.5%) implies roughly +0.3% to +3.7% annualized 10-year growth versus a 7-9%/yr base case, i.e. the stock is cheap on the analyst's own work, though with a thinner margin of safety than CAH given the higher recent debt load and impairment pattern.

kill: Adjusted EPS growth falls below 4% for two consecutive quarters (vs the ~5–7% long-term target)
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA rises above 6.0x without a credit-positive equity issuance offsetting it
A state commission (Georgia, Alabama or Mississippi PSC) formally disallows recovery of a material capex or fuel-cost item (>$250mn) in a rate order
Guidance is cut (not just reaffirmed) at any of the next two quarterly releases
A confirmed hyperscaler data-center load agreement in the Southeast is publicly cancelled or downsized
adverse: Guidance track record not independently verified this pass (no confirmed prior-range comparison from a primary source) - treat as medium, not high, confidence
Consolidated net debt/EBITDA ~5.2x leaves limited headroom before the next rate case
1-year price momentum negative (-4.1%) versus peers that have already re-rated on confirmed hyperscaler contracts
rows.thesis: Southeast's largest regulated utility, Vogtle risk now behind it, priced fairly while real data-center demand growth is still barely in the price.

val_consistency.reconciliation: SO has no row in v1_valuation_table.csv, so there is no systematic verdict to reconcile against. This dossier's own reverse-DCF (NTM P/E 17.1x, ~7% cost of equity) implies ~1% perpetual growth, well below SO's ~5-7% long-term guided growth (implied_vs_base = below), which is why the verdict is INCLUDE rather than WATCH despite a non-cheap 17.1x multiple.

kill: Nonperforming-asset ratio rises above 1.00% (vs 0.85% at 2Q26) for two consecutive quarters.
CET1 ratio falls below 9.5% (reported) without a disclosed pause in buybacks.
Adjusted ROTCE fails to reach 17% by 4Q26 (management's own implied bar - full earnings power clearly evident by Q4).
Net charge-off ratio rises above 0.45% for two consecutive quarters (vs 0.25% at 2Q26).
Efficiency ratio fails to improve below 58% by 1Q27 (vs 61.5% at 2Q26, post both systems conversions).
adverse: Nonperforming-asset ratio rose for two straight quarters (0.72% -> 0.85%, 1Q26 -> 2Q26) even as net charge-offs stayed low.
CET1 10.0% (adjusted 9.0%), both down sequentially, while buybacks continued ($159mm in 2Q26) - less capital cushion than FITB if credit surprises.
2Q26 GAAP EPS of $0.33 includes $152mm of pre-tax acquisition-related Notable Items; adjusted EPS was $0.39.
rows.thesis: Midwest regional bank that just finished integrating two Texas/South mergers, with margins and book value already rising while the stock still prices in almost no growth.

val_consistency.reconciliation: No V1 systematic valuation row exists for HBAN. Own P/TBV excess-return reverse-DCF (1.62x TBV, ~16% assumed long-run adjusted ROTCE, 10% cost of equity) implies the market is pricing only ~0-1% perpetual growth, well below the analyst's own mid-single-digit base case -> below/cheap.

note: Weights are shares of the stock sleeve. Sleeve rules were fixed before the diligence verdicts were read: official point-in-time score in the top 70, 1-year volatility ≤ 45%, no pending takeover, valuation attractive or fair versus the company's own history, diligence INCLUDE (full) or INCLUDE-SMALL (half), ≤ 2 names per sub-industry, inverse-volatility weights of 3–10% (full conviction) or 1.5–5% (half conviction), sectors ≤ 25%; sleeve capacity the caps cannot absorb is held in the S&P 500 index fund. * Calibrated odds are empirical frequencies for S&P 500 stocks in the same score decile and volatility band, 2011–2025.
